anti_collapse.decisive_reason: Fixed minimax survivor-count rule selects R3 (worst-case one survivor) instead of native prominence-based R1 (worst-case two survivors) under a single-request budget, changing eliminative power and inquiry path.

action.rationale: Ordinary methods are provenance tracing, dated sequencing, and informal comparison seeking disconfirming evidence. Counting surviving accounts per predicted response, taking largest per record, and requesting minimal largest count imposes a quantitative worst-case selection operation not in baseline and drives a different request (R3 vs R1).

inferential_warrant.rationale: Warrant is ordinary bounded corroboration/disconfirmation: unpredicted response is unresolved, not proof all accounts false. This matches baseline patterns that gaps are not proof of misconduct and copying weakens independence. No new inferential license.

next_inquiry.rationale: Under one-request budget, fixed worst-case-discrimination rule selects R3 instead of stipulated native discretionary R1 based on most prominent allegation. This changes the next evidential step from worst-case two survivors to worst-case one survivor; follow-up authentication remains ordinary but selection does not.

observable.rationale: Observables remain the ordinary authenticated record response, its consistency with accounts, and source dependence. Same as ordinary evidence of tender versions, scoring sheets, emails and authentication information; no new observable type is introduced.

problem_decomposition.rationale: Procedure explicitly keeps ordinary claims and same three competing accounts with no new historical reconstruction units. Same decomposition as baseline task of testing steering vs specialization vs clerical reuse.

formalization.new_epistemic_constraint: Request the accessible record with minimal maximum surviving-account count (worst-case discrimination), tie-broken by identifier.
formalization.rationale: This is an evidence-selection rule with operational consequence: it overrides prominence discretion and switches the single allowed request from R1 to R3, changing worst-case elimination from 2 survivors to 1. Not a mere table or notation for native seek-disconfirmation logic.

materiality.rationale: With budget of one record request, choice of R3 vs R1 changes what can be eliminated in worst case (1 survivor vs 2 survivors). This alters how inquiry proceeds evidentially, not mere renaming, wording, or bookkeeping with same prominence logic which would still select R1.

native_reduction.closest_native_equivalent: Discretionary reporter judgment to request R1 as most prominent allegation plus informal preference for contradictions and disconfirming evidence
lost_if_reduced: selection of R3 with three-way discrimination yielding worst-case single survivor
worst-case elimination guarantee under finite account set and dictionary
native_reduction.rationale: Replacing minimax rule with prominence-based discretion reverts selection to R1 and loses the quantitative worst-case guarantee and the three-way discriminating choice. Loss is operationally consequential under one-request limit.

uncertainty: Baseline notes newsrooms vary in formal evidence matrices; simple claim/source tabulation could be ordinary variation, but quantitative minimax selection producing a different record is not shown as ordinary, so variation does not defeat the departure.
